text:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran an int4 drop-in for ventus9b v1.1 on the canary pool. Observed p95+p99 latency regression (~+6% p95, spikes at p99) and 3 OOMs during a 1h burst. Memory fragmentation looks suspicious. attaching perf links and logs: https://perf.internal/ventus9b/v1.1 :eyes:
sanjay: Which batching and gen defaults did you use? max_new_tokens, prefetch, microbatch?
maya: Canary used: BATCH_SIZE=8, MICRO_BATCH=1, MAX_NEW_TOKENS=256, PREFETCH=enabled. Kernel set is int4-optimized-archA. Small snippet from the canary config:
```yaml
model: ventus9b
version: v1.1-int4-dropin
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  micro_batch: 1
generation:
  max_new_tokens: 256
prefetch: true
kv_trim_threshold: 0.5
```
liam: Ok. Two quick hypotheses: 1) the int4 kernel is allocating a transient workspace that's not freed fast causing fragmentation under burst. 2) our default max_new_tokens=256 increases KV usage and amplifies frag on this model.
sanjay: Agreed. Try lowering max_new_tokens default to 128 for the canary and reduce max_batch_size to 4. Also disable prefetch for the first run to remove that variable.
liam: Also recommend bumping kv_trim_threshold to 0.6 and enable slot compactor patch (PR #4123) which consolidates freed slabs quicker. Patch link: https://git.internal/r/4123
maya: Starting canary run with: max_batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=128, prefetch=false, kv_trim_threshold=0.6 + slot compactor. ETA ~30m. I'll post logs.
infra-bot: canary-deploy: ventus9b v1.1-int4-dropin trial-42 rolled to 3 hosts (h21,h22,h23) — rollout complete.
maya: Initial 20m smoke: 0 OOMs, p95 back to baseline, p99 tail still ~+3%. CPU on host h22 shows higher memcpy activity during decode — possible memcpy hotspot in the int4 kernel.
liam: If memcpy is the hotspot, try switching to the alternative transpose kernel (int4-transpose-v2) that reduces intermediate copies. It trades a tiny CPU for less GPU-side fragmentation. Can we A/B that?
maya: Kicking an A/B: half hosts run transpose-v2 kernel, half keep current. Will reconvene with 2h run results.
sanjay: Thanks — if we still see tail, we can consider making max_new_tokens model default 128 for ventus9b and add an onboarding note in the model catalog about preferred batching and kernel. :memo:
maya: Noted. Will add a short blurb to the model onboarding doc and the console recommendations if A/B shows improvement.
